source_observations.description: The llama grazes, then the native edit cuts to its face against blue mountain layers.

observability_rules.stable_interval: A stable-effect claim requires the unchanged 1000 ms continuous interval with observable target evidence. Do not bridge complete target absence or combine disconnected glimpses. This sampling audit alone does not certify every frame of such an interval.

At 12.080 s hair top, hands and glass reappear; 12.160–13.600 s sampled views largely expose upper head/eyes and hands. At 14.400 s hair/back and an arm are visible; at 14.480 s only the raised hand/forearm remnant is visible. At 14.880 s head and upper torso return. One ornate landscape panel; target crosses left/center/right in front of animated ribbons, flowers and heart/globe graphics. The black-clad man remains a separate identity.

source_observations.description: Head, neck, yellow long-sleeved torso and gesturing arms/hands are usually visible. At 10.400 s, bent dark-blue trouser legs and pink footwear are visible during a jump, but the raised hand is clipped by the upper frame. At 11.840 s only hair tips remain; at 11.920 and 12.000 s fingertips remain above the lower frame. At 12.000 s a wine glass also remains. At 12.080 s hair top, hands and glass reappear; 12.160–13.600 s sampled views largely expose upper head/eyes and hands. At 14.400 s hair/back and an arm are visible; at 14.480 s only the raised hand/forearm remnant is visible. At 14.880 s head and upper torso return. One ornate landscape panel; target crosses left/center/right in front of animated ribbons, flowers and heart/globe graphics. The black-clad man remains a separate identity.

Head returns at 81.880 s in a small upper-left panel. At 82.600 s only upper head/eyes are exposed; 83 s views place face/torso in a lower-left panel, then lower-middle panel. A multi-panel collage with head/torso distributed across separate frames becomes a large single panel. Purple birds, musical notes, rainbow, drum/skeleton art, volcano, man’s separate fragments, frame borders and black gutters are all protected.

source_observations.description: The unedited source shows two complete woven cushions on the same window bench: dark blue at screen left and pale gray at screen right, with a clear gap. The original terracotta floor pot, shutters, chipped plaster, side doorway and rug remain visible. Outdoor foliage and dappled shadows move. The framing changes gently rather than remaining pixel-locked. A small defocused foreground leaf briefly overlaps a small area of the left cushion near 2.1-2.4 seconds; it does not replace or reshape the cushion in the inspected evidence.

Both complete cushions remain visible and retain their left/right roles and basic square geometry. Slow global reframing and moving foliage/shadows continue. A cumulative warm-to-pink cast becomes more noticeable across the bench, plaster and pot. Small foreground leaf flecks appear intermittently, including a brief small overlap on the left cushion around the sampled 17-second frame; the right cushion remains plainly distinguishable from the left cushion.

The right cushion is still the unedited pale-gray source cushion under the current lighting; the left cushion remains dark blue. Neither cushion disappears in the inspected full-frame samples, including every frame from 24 through 25 seconds. The scene retains its current gentle camera trajectory, accumulated pink/warm cast, leaf-shadow motion and occasional small foreground leaves. No orange or pale-green cushion edit is present in this source. Restoration must use the contemporaneous source frame at matching PTS, not the opening frame. At the final frame n=719 (29.958333 seconds), the terracotta pot remains identifiable but its outer left contour and the left end of its rim are slightly clipped by image x=0. Both cushions remain fully visible. Preserve the source-visible pot contour and current framing at matching PTS; do not invent hidden pot pixels or require its complete opening-frame silhouette. The exact onset of this edge clipping has not been established.
